data.why: The app has no file-upload widget; the scientist pastes a protein sequence into a text area, and a hardcoded p53 fragment is already built into app.py behind a 'Load example (p53)' button.

goals: Paste a protein sequence of interest and get a phosphorylation probability for every S/T/Y residue
Identify which candidate sites are predicted phosphosites at a chosen decision threshold
Inspect the occlusion-based importance profile for a specific site to see which neighbouring residues drove the prediction
Compare predictions and explanations across different proteins or protein variants by pasting new sequences
Sanity-check the model's behavior on a known, published example (p53 N-terminal fragment) before trusting it on a novel sequence

review.summary: The predict-and-threshold half of LitePhospho is mapped accurately, at the right depth and with good wording. Every screen I opened supports its node, apart from one mis-stated input-cleaning claim. But the explanation that gives the tool its name is absent from the tree and the features because of a fixable pyarrow/NumPy deployment error, so the tree needs a re-run of that phase and the listed corrections before filing.
